title: Playlist and Recipe
premise: Cyrus Underhill has survived small-town Montana by keeping his head down, counting the 214 days until graduation and escaping to a city where nobody knows him. When he finds his late grandmother's recipe box, one card isn't a recipe at all: it's a set of directions — and following them pulls him into a hidden network of people his grandmother protected for decades. As Cyrus uncovers what she risked and who she saved, he must decide whether to keep her secrets and his own, or tell the truth even if it costs him his best friend and the fragile safety of the town. The price of survival, he learns, is paid in full only when you stop surviving and start living; the book ends with Cyrus staying, choosing love and found family over the escape he'd been counting toward.
about_author: Wendell Amberdale is a former small-town librarian who spent a decade collecting the recipes and rumors of rural America before turning to fiction. They write about queer kids in places that were never built for them, and about the quiet heroism of grandmothers.

chapters.title: Two Hundred and Fourteen
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Opening day of senior year in Halloway, population nine hundred. Cyrus catalogs the town's small cruelties and his countdown calendar, establishing his only anchor: Sunday dinners at his grandmother's house. Beat: weary endurance, the sense of a sentence being served.

chapters.title: The Card That Isn't Food
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. After Grandma Ruth's sudden death, Cyrus sorts her recipe box for the estate sale and finds a card labeled 'For When It's Time' — directions to a cellar beneath the old grain elevator, not ingredients. Beat: grief sharpened into curiosity, the first crack in his ordinary world.

chapters.title: Cellar Light
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Following the directions at midnight, Cyrus finds a hidden room with supplies, false documents, and a ledger of names — including his grandmother's handwriting next to dates spanning fifty years. Someone is living there now. Beat: awe and fear colliding.

chapters.title: Marisol
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. He catches a teenage girl, Marisol, raiding the cellar — a runaway his grandmother's network was sheltering. Marisol doesn't trust him, and he can't explain why he's here. Beat: prickly first contact; two survivors circling.

chapters.title: Denny Knows Something
chapters.summary: Denny's POV. Cyrus's best friend since second grade has noticed the midnight trips and the boxes Cyrus is moving. Denny, whose father is the county sheriff, covers for Cyrus once — then starts asking questions he shouldn't. Beat: loyalty tested before the stakes are even clear.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus decodes the ledger: his grandmother hid people for decades — draft resisters, abused wives, queer kids like him. He finds his own name, written when he was twelve, with the note 'when he's ready.' Beat: revelation that reframes his whole childhood.

chapters.title: Recipe for Two
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Marisol and Cyrus cook together from Ruth's real recipes, and she tells him why she ran. The kitchen becomes the first place Cyrus has ever been fully himself. Beat: warmth, found family beginning to form, the countdown calendar quietly ignored.

chapters.title: The Sheriff's Dinner
chapters.summary: Denny's POV. Denny's father mentions a missing-persons bulletin matching Marisol and a 'suspicious activity' report at the grain elevator. Denny lies to his father's face for the first time. Beat: dread; the noose of duty tightening around friendship.

chapters.title: Ninety-Nine Days
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. With graduation approaching, Cyrus faces a choice: the scholarship in Seattle or staying to keep the network alive. He tells no one, but he stops crossing days off. Beat: the escape dream curdling into a question he can't answer.

chapters.title: What Ruth Promised
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol finds letters revealing Ruth promised every person she sheltered one thing: 'You will be believed here.' Marisol, who has never been believed anywhere, decides to trust Cyrus with the whole truth. Beat: vulnerability as courage.

chapters.title: The Second Card
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A second hidden card surfaces: instructions for 'when the house is full' — a plan to move everyone out at once, requiring someone local with a clean record and a truck. Ruth wrote Cyrus's name on it years ago. Beat: the weight of a legacy he never asked for.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Elevator
chapters.summary: Denny's POV. Denny follows Cyrus and catches him mid-extraction. Cornered, Cyrus tells him everything — the cellar, the ledger, Marisol. Denny's response isn't anger but terror: his father will find out, and Denny will have to choose. Beat: the truth told, the friendship cracking under it.

chapters.title: Silence Between Friends
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A week of silence. Cyrus prepares the move alone; Denny wrestles at home, his father growing suspicious, a deputy sniffing around the elevator. Beat: the cost of honesty arriving on schedule.

chapters.title: The Deputy's Flashlight
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. A deputy nearly discovers the cellar during a school-day sweep. Marisol hides in the dark while he reads Ruth's ledger aloud, mocking it. Something in her hardens: she's done being hidden. Beat: fear transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: Denny's Decision
chapters.summary: Denny's POV. Denny finds his father's file on the 'grain elevator person' and realizes his father intends to detain Marisol regardless of her safety. Denny copies the file and brings it to Cyrus. Beat: duty inverted — loyalty to people over institution.

chapters.title: Moving Day
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The network moves at dawn: Marisol and two others Ruth was still sheltering go north in Cyrus's truck, following the second card's route. It nearly works. Beat: adrenaline, competence, the found family functioning as one body.

chapters.title: Roadblock
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The sheriff waits at the county line. Denny steps between the trucks and his father and tells the truth — all of it, in front of everyone. Marisol speaks her own name and her own story. Beat: climax; truth as the only weapon left.

chapters.title: The Price
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The fallout: Cyrus loses the scholarship's local sponsor, Denny is estranged from his father, the town splits into whispering camps. Cyrus reads Ruth's ledger aloud at the public hearing, name by name. Beat: grief and cost, honestly counted.

chapters.title: Believed Here
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol, now safe with allies two counties over, sends Cyrus a letter: 'She promised I'd be believed. You kept it.' Cyrus realizes the network doesn't end with Ruth — it continues with whoever says yes. Beat: inheritance accepted.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus walks at graduation with the countdown calendar unopened in his pocket. Denny sits with him, not with his father. The town that watched him survive now watches him be seen. Beat: quiet triumph; the sentence served, the prisoner free.

chapters.title: The Empty Card
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. In the recipe box, Cyrus finds one last blank card and Ruth's pen. He writes the first line of a new set of directions — for the next kid who needs a cellar, a kitchen, a name that's believed. Beat: legacy made deliberate.

chapters.title: Playlist for Staying
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, epilogue. Summer. Cyrus burns a CD for Marisol, restocks the cellar, and makes Sunday dinner for the small found family that remains. He isn't leaving for the city; he's building one here. Beat: love against duty resolved — he chooses both, and they turn out to be the same thing.
